text: data.10,13,15 Compared with the films prepared by solution casting, the enhancement of the enthalpy change in the ES film may be explained by the possibility of forming microparticles or nanoparticles when the concentration of the solution varies between 2% to 10%.38 In this case, the sufficient surface tension of the particles favors the entanglement of polymer chains, and the particle deposition also increases the potential to produce chain entanglement.39,40 Substantial movement of polymer chains may be lower in ES films due to polymer entanglement, which can restricts the mobility of polymer chains to frustrate the free movement of polymer chains. The increase in difficulty in chain movement may lead to a higher energy requirement for melting, resulting in a higher melting enthalpy. It is noted that the spray processing in other studies is different from the electrospray technique. However, a spray process is well-known to create polymer entanglement38 but the degree of entanglement will not be discussed in this work. In addition, the rapid evaporation of solvent on the ES film may also limit the mobility of the terpolymer chain from MPs, so the higher rigidity of the chains might also be attributed to the enhancement of enthalpy compared with SC films. It's also noted that the surface morphology of the ES films after annealed 120˚C for 18h was different than SC films (Figure 6). While the crystallite sizes are similar for both films annealed 17 DE-EE0009099 at 120˚C (Table 1), the direction of the crystallites appears different, with the aggregate crystallites on the surface of the ES film (Figure 6a) appearing less randomly aligned than on the SC films (Figure 6c). An ImageJ program was used to characterize the orientation of the crystallites. Three locations on the SEM images of ES A120 (Figure 6b) were selected from the aggregates, and the direction of the crystallites presented on the ES films were 72˚  9˚, 103˚  7˚, and 70˚  6˚. However, the direction of the crystallites presented on SC A120 were 36˚  19˚, 156˚  11˚, and 35˚  11˚ based on the selected locations in Figure 6d. The ES films annealed at 120˚C tend to have the crystallites aggregated and the direction analysis contains showed less variation (i.e. a lower standard deviation in the direction measurement) that implies a more uniform directionality in the aggregate than crystallites observed on the surface of SC films that were annealed at 120˚C.
